1#main: The laws of proofreading a Sefer Torah and not leaving it in error. In it are 8 seifim. A Sefer Torah that is not proofread—it is forbidden to leave it more than thirty days, but one must correct it or put it in genizah. (And the same law applies to other books) (Rashi and Beit Yosef in the name of Hagahos Maimoniyos and Rabbenu Yerucham, Netiv 50). And one may not proofread any book by reasoning alone, but only by clear sight that there is an error in it (Rav R' David Cohen, Beit Tov, and ancient cherem).
2#main: If they read from a Sefer Torah in public and an error was found in it—they bring out another Sefer Torah and begin from the place where the error was found, and complete the seven for those who read in error. And if the error was found in the middle of the Torah reading, he finishes his reading in the valid book and recites the blessing after it; and he does not recite the blessing before it, for the blessing he recited before was on the invalid Sefer Torah; and likewise the reading they read in it is valid for them b'dieved. {Rama: And there is no difference whether the error was found in the first Sefer Torah or in the second with which they read the day's obligation for maftir (and see in Orach Chaim siman 143).}
3#main: A Sefer Torah in which three errors were found—it is forbidden to read from it until they proofread it, for it is presumed erroneous.
4#main: A Sefer Torah that has three errors on every page—one corrects it; and if there were four, one puts it in genizah. And if the majority of the book was proofread and the remainder has four errors on every page, and even one page remains from that remainder corrupted without four errors—this one is corrected. When does this apply? When he wrote plene what should be defective, for it is disgraceful to hang so much between lines; but if he wrote defective what should be plene, even if there are several errors on every page, one corrects it, for scraping is not as disgraceful as hanging. {Rama: And when scraping, he widens the letter before and after it somewhat so the place of scraping not be a break in the word (Beit Yosef and Mordechai, beginning of Hilchos Ketanim).}
5#main: If he skipped two or three lines, he should not erase three lines to write in their place four or five to insert what he skipped, because he diminishes the writing and it appears like erasure (meaning: like the skin of a leopard that has many shades). And it is good to remove the sheet (nevertheless scribes are accustomed to correct, as explained above at the beginning of siman 275).
